id_verification

id_verification.Rmd

The problem

Most studies that require ohcleandat involve collecting and integrating multiple dataset stored in different formats (csv, excel, googlesheets, redcap, ODK, etc.). Before two or more datasets can be integrated, the IDs that link them (foreign keys) have to be validated.

Some mismatches are expected in field-collected data: a household recorded in a sampling roster but not yet in the survey, a household opts out of a component of the the study, or a sample from a household is lost and cannot be used in a serosurvey. These are all legitimate reasons a linking ID may not be present in a particular dataset. However, some IDs may not match because of data entry errors - a typo, a record entered twice - any number of issues can arise during collection. Both expected and unexpected mismatches need to be validated to ensure high quality data integration.

create_id_log() takes two “semi-clean” datasets and returns a validation log — one row per problem ID, formatted so a human can review it, decide what the correct value is, and initial the change. The function checks for two classes of problem: IDs that exist in one dataset but not the other, and IDs that appear more than once within a single dataset.

Example data

Two small datasets linked by household ID. The household file uses hh_id; the individual roster calls the same thing household_id.

households <- tibble::tibble(
  hh_record = 1:5,
  hh_id     = c("H001", "H002", "H003", "H004", "H002"),
  village   = c("Kisumu", "Kisumu", "Siaya", "Siaya", "Kisumu")
)

sampling_roster <- tibble::tibble(
  person_record = 1:5,
  household_id  = c("H001", "H002", "H002", "H005", "H006"),
  age           = c(34, 12, 41, 27, 8)
)

H003 and H004 have no one in the sampling roster. H005 and H006 are in the sampling roster but not in the household file. Those four are what we want flagged as cross-dataset mismatches. In addition, H002 appears twice in the household file — that duplicate is flagged separately.

Creating the log 

id_log <- ohcleandat::create_id_log(
  semiclean_x   = households,
  semiclean_y   = roster,
  by            = c("hh_id" = "household_id"),
  primary_key_x = "hh_record",
  primary_key_y = "person_record",
  name_x        = "data/raw/households_2026.csv",
  name_y        = "data/raw/roster_2026.csv"
)

id_log

Each row is one problem ID. The columns are:

Column What it holds
dataset Which file the problem ID came from
entry The primary key of the offending row, so you can find it
field The ID column being checked
issue A plain-language description of the mismatch or duplication
old_value The ID as it currently appears
no_change, new_val, user_initials, comments Blank — filled in by the reviewer

The last four are intentionally empty. The log is meant to be written out, handed to whoever knows the data, and returned with decisions recorded.

Duplicate IDs

In addition to cross-dataset mismatches, create_id_log() checks each dataset independently for IDs that appear more than once. Duplicates are flagged in the same log under a distinct issue description, so a reviewer sees all ID problems in one place.

A duplicate row in the log does not mean the record should be deleted. It means the same ID was recorded more than once and a human needs to decide whether the two rows represent the same event entered twice, or two genuinely different records that were assigned the same ID by mistake. The reviewer uses no_change and new_val to record that decision, just as they would for a cross-dataset mismatch.

# H002 appears twice in households — both rows will appear in the log
# with issue = "household_id in dataset_x does not match any HHID in dataset_y"
id_log |>
  dplyr::filter(grepl("does not match", issue))

When the same ID is duplicated in both datasets, two separate rows appear in the log — one flagged against each dataset — so the reviewer can assess each side independently.

Handing it off for review 

readr::write_csv(id_log, "logs/id_validation_2026-08-19.csv")

A reviewer marks no_change for IDs that are legitimately absent (a household that genuinely enrolled no one) with a “T” or “True”, or enters a “F” or “False” and fills new_val with the corrected ID where it’s a typo. user_initials and comments keep the audit trail. The same convention applies to duplicates: if both rows are legitimate, the reviewer assigns a corrected ID to one of them in new_val; if one is a true duplicate entry, they mark it no_change = "T" to indicate it can be dropped.

Matching columns with the same name

When both datasets use the same column name, by is just a string:

create_id_log(
  semiclean_x   = households,
  semiclean_y   = roster,
  by            = "hh_id",
  primary_key_x = "hh_record",
  primary_key_y = "person_record",
  name_x        = "households.csv",
  name_y        = "roster.csv"
)

# by is a character variable containing match id, or if named different, 
# a named character vector like c("a" = "b")
# this function assumes that the named character vector follows the convention of
# c("variable in semiclean_x" = "variable in semiclean_y")

Combining logs across multiple datasets

create_id_log() does pairwise comparisons of datasets, which is fine when there aren’t very many datasets that share a foreign key, but when the same ID appears across several files — a household ID shared by the survey, the roster, seroprevalance data, environmental data, mosquito trapping data, and the visit records — making sure you capture all unique pairwise comparisons across all the datasets becomes difficult.

# number of unique pairs for 6 datasets
utils::combn(1:6,2,simplify = FALSE) |>
  length()
#> [1] 15

To handle more complex comparisons, use the create_full_id_log() function. This function takes a list of datasets, computes the number of unique pairs, and returns a combined id validation log for all pairs.

# Here we make a list of six datasets and run the pairwise comparison for all 6
# using create_full_id_log()


survey <- list(
  semiclean_data = data.frame(primary_key = 1:10,
                              foreign_key = letters[1:10],
                              do_you_like_ohcleandat = sample(c("yes","no"),size = 10,replace = TRUE)),
  foreign_key = "foreign_key",
  primary_key = "primary_key",
  name = "survey"
)


roster <- list(
  semiclean_data = data.frame(primary_key = 1:10,
                              foreign_key = letters[1:10],
                              gender = sample(c("man","woman","prefer not to say"),10,replace = TRUE)),
  foreign_key = "foreign_key",
  primary_key = "primary_key",
  name = "roster"
)


sero_prev <- list(
  semiclean_data = data.frame(sample_id = 1:10,
                              hhid = letters[2:11],
                              pos = sample(c(TRUE,FALSE),size = 10, replace = TRUE)),
  foreign_key = "hhid",
  primary_key = "sample_id",
  name = "sero_prev"
)


env_data <- list(
  semiclean_data = data.frame(measurement_id = 1:10,
                              house_hold_id = c(rep(letters[1],2),letters[3:10])
  ),
  foreign_key = "house_hold_id",
  primary_key = "measurement_id",
  name = "env_data.csv"
)

mos_data <- list(
  semiclean_data = data.frame(mosquito_id = 1:10,
                              hhold_id = c(rep(letters[1],2),letters[3:10]),
                              genus = sample(c("Aedes","Culex"),10,TRUE)
  ),
  foreign_key = "hhold_id",
  primary_key = "mosquito_id",
  name = "mos_data"
)


visit_record <- list(
  semiclean_data = data.frame(visit_id = 1:5,
                              hhid = c(rep(letters[1],2),letters[3:5]),
                              construction_material = sample(c("stick","straw","brick"), 5,TRUE)
  ),
  foreign_key = "hhid",
  primary_key = "visit_id",
  name = "visit_record"
)

dataset_list <- list(survey,roster,sero_prev,env_data,mos_data,visit_record)

hhid_id_int_log  <- create_full_id_log(dataset_list) |>
  head(n = 10)

The output schema is the same every time, and the dataset column identifies where each flagged ID came from, so a combined log reads as one review task rather than several. Which pairs to run is a study design question, not a technical one: if one file serves as the authoritative source of IDs, compare each of the others against it and leave it at that; if the files are meant to be integrated in sequence, compare each pair in the order they will be joined. Comparing every possible pair is an option, but on more than three or four datasets it produces overlapping rows that ask a reviewer to resolve the same ID more than once. Match the set of comparisons to the integration you actually intend to perform.

Where this fits

create_id_log() is another checking step that gets integrated into the ohcleandat cleaning mechanics. The intended loop is: run the log, review it, apply the corrections to your semi-clean files, then run it again. When all the issues within the log have been resolved, the cleaning task is complete.

This is a highly simplified example, in practice you may want to use separate targets files if you are working with many datasets.

Potential file structure

- _targets.R
- _intregration_targets.R
- _survey_targets.R
- _mos_targets.R
...
library(dm)

# lets pretend this is what our data look like
survey_data <- data.frame(hhid = letters[1:10],
                          some_question = rbinom(n = 10,size = 1,prob = .3))

mos_data <- data.frame(mos_id = as.character(1:10),
                       genus = sample(c("Aedes","Culex"),size = 10,replace = TRUE),
                       env_id = paste("env",1:10,sep = "_"),
                       household_id = sample(letters[1:10],10))

env_data <- data.frame(env_id = paste("env",1:10,sep = "_"),
                       trap_id = 1:10,
                       hhid = toupper(mos_data$household_id))

project_data_no_keys <- dm::dm(survey_data,mos_data,env_data)

# add primary keys
project_data_pks <- project_data_no_keys |>
   dm::dm_add_pk(table = survey_data, columns = hhid) |>
   dm::dm_add_pk(table = mos_data, columns = mos_id) |>
   dm::dm_add_pk(table = env_data, columns = env_id) 

# have dm look for foreign keys
dm::dm_enum_fk_candidates(project_data_pks,table = mos_data,ref_table = survey_data)

## add foreign keys

project_data_fks <- project_data_pks |>
  dm::dm_add_fk(table = mos_data,columns = "household_id", ref_table = survey_data) |>
  dm::dm_add_fk(table = mos_data,columns = "env_id", ref_table = env_data) |>
  dm::dm_add_fk(table = env_data,columns = "hhid", ref_table = survey_data) |>
  dm::dm_add_fk(table = env_data,columns = "trap_id", ref_table = mos_data) 

# look at the data model
dm::dm_get_all_fks(project_data_fks)

# pak::pak("rich-iannone/DiagrammeR@v1.0.11") and restart if diagram doesnt work.

project_data_fks |>
  dm::dm_draw()


# get all of the id logs and combine them into a single dataset
int_log_targets <- tar_plan(
  # read in id validation logs
  tar_target(hhid_log, get_dropbox_val_logs("hhid_log.csv"), 
             path_name = "my_cool_project/validation_logs"),
  tar_target(mos_id_log, get_dropbox_val_logs("mos_id_log.csv"),
             path_name = "my_cool_project/validation_logs"),
  tar_target(env_id_log, get_dropbox_val_logs("env_id_log.csv"),
             path_name = "my_cool_project/validation_logs"),
  tar_target(mos_id_log, get_dropbox_val_logs("mos_id_log.csv"),
             path_name = "my_cool_project/validation_logs")
  # rbind logs
  tar_target(all_ids_existing_log, rbind(hhid_log,human_id_log,animal_id_log,mos_id_log))
  
)


survey_data <- tar_plan(
  
  # read raw data
  tar_target(
    survey_data_raw,
    get_odk_responses(url ="https://odk.xyz.io/v1/projects/5/forms/survey.svc",
                      un = Sys.getenv("ODK_USERNAME"),
                      pw = Sys.getenv("ODK_PASSWORD"),
                      odkc_version = Sys.getenv("ODKC_VERSION")
    )
  ),
  # read in dataset validation log
  tar_target(survey_existing_log, get_dropbox_val_logs(file_name = "survey_log.csv",
                                                       path_name = "my_cool_project/validation_logs")),
  # join the existing validation log to the id validation log with `join_id_log`
  tar_target(survey_log_with_ids, join_id_log(existing_log = survey_existing_log,
                                              id_log = all_ids_existing_log,
                                              dataset_name = "survey_data" ))
  # make semi_clean data
  targets::tar_target(
    survey_data_semiclean,
    ohcleandat::correct_data(
      validation_log = survey_log_with_ids,
      data = survey_data_raw,
      primary_key = "key"
    )
  ),
  
  # see mechanics vignette
  # upload semiclean data
  # create rules
  # make validation log
  
  
)

mosquito_data <- tar_plan(
  # read raw data
  # read in dataset validation log
  # join the existing validation log to the id validation log with `join_id_log`
  # make semi_clean data
  # upload semiclean data
  # create rules
  # make validation log
)


env_data <- tar_plan(
  # read raw data
  # read in dataset validation log
  # join the existing validation log to the id validation log with `join_id_log`
  # make semi_clean data
  # upload semiclean data
  # create rules
  # make validation log
  
)

# make the id validation log from semi-clean data
# combine new with existing using combine log
# upload 


integration_targets <- tar_plan(
  # make the household id log (hhid) across all three datasets
  # create the dataset list with the semiclean data. create_hhid_dataset_list is a custom function.
  tar_target(dataset_list_hhid,
             create_hhid_dataset_list(survey_semiclean,mos_semiclean,env_semiclean)
  ),
  # make new full id log 
  tar_target(hhid_id_log_new, 
             create_full_id_log(dataset_list_hhid)
  ),
  # combine with previous id log
  tar_target(hhid_log_combined,
             combine_logs(hhid_log,hhid_id_log_new,is_id_log = TRUE)),
  # upload combined log
  targets::tar_target(
    upload_id_verification_targets,
    ohcleandat::dropbox_upload(
      log = hhid_log_combined,
      file_path = here::here("outputs/hhid_id_log.csv"),
      dropbox_path = "dropbox/validation_logs"
    ),
    cue = targets::tar_cue("always")
  )
  # mos id
  # env id
  
)
